limits: This checks the description of one explicitly cited scenario study, not whether the scenario is the true counterfactual.  The study holds other generation capacity fixed, omits grid-related curtailment and some wider economic effects, and says alternative investment responses could reduce the price effect. Neither correction proves that preserving feed-in support is unwise or that a specific household actually realised the modelled saving. No intent is inferred.
materiality_explanation: Minor: an auxiliary numerical/source-description issue in a much broader submission. The cited scenario still finds substantial solar benefits and the policy conclusion does not depend on this error alone.

card.law_is_about: Renewable-electricity support and marketing rules, including small rooftop systems.
card.they_want: Preserve the fixed feed-in tariff for rooftop solar.
card.they_claim: The cited scenario makes 2025 electricity prices 20 percent higher without solar.
card.the_problem: Its detailed figures imply about 26.3 percent higher without solar;20.8 percent is the reduction in the reverse direction.

claim_quote.original: um durchschnittlich 20 Prozent höher gewesen wäre
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation of fragment: would have been 20 percent higher on average

locator.section: Staatliche Förderung für Photovoltaik kommt Wirtschaft und allen Verbrauchern zugute, first paragraph

counter_quote.original: entspricht einer Reduktion von 20,8 % durch die Erzeugung aus Photovoltaik.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation of fragment: corresponds to a 20.8 percent reduction due to generation from photovoltaics.

locator.section: 2025 – Veränderung der Strompreise und ihrer Struktur, lower-left explanation and adjoining bar chart

correction: The detailed study chart gives 112.8€/MWh withoutPV and 89.3€/MWh withPV. The reverse comparison is(112.8−89.3)/89.3≈26.32 percent higher withoutPV. The 20.8 percent reduction uses 112.8 as denominator. Preserve the absolute 23.5€/MWh difference.
effect: The printed percentage understates the modelled no-solar price increase; correction strengthens this supporting pro-solar point rather than weakening it.
direction_explanation: False: the corrected increase is larger and therefore supports the request more strongly. This is separate from minor severity.
context_and_alternatives: Important source qualification: the primary study’s own summary on physical 2 describes about 21 percent higher withoutPV. The submission therefore follows a source-summary formulation rather than inventing the direction. The detailed chart and reduction explanation on 7 are internally more precise.
Rounding or general shorthand can explain the 20/21 difference, but cannot make a 20.8 percent reduction identical to a 20.8 percent increase with the other baseline.
No claim is made that the counterfactual price itself was observed or that one static scenario establishes the best support policy.
